Ribbon.tips.circlediameter: Creates a circle using a center point and a diameter
Ribbon.tips.circle2p: Creates a circle using two endpoints of the diameter
Ribbon.tips.circle3p: Creates a circle using three points on the circumference
Ribbon.tips.arc: Creates an arc using three points
Ribbon.tips.arcsce: Creates an arc using the start point, center, and endpoint
Ribbon.tips.arccse: Creates an arc using a center point, start point, and a third point that determines the endpoint
Ribbon.tips.ellipsecenter: Creates an ellipse using a specified center point
Ribbon.tips.ellipse: Creates an ellipse or an elliptical arc

Ribbon.tips.splinefit: Draws a spline with fit points
Ribbon.tips.splinecv: Draws a spline with control vertices
Ribbon.tips.xline: Creates a line of infinite length
Ribbon.tips.ray: Creates a line that starts at a point and continues to infinity
Ribbon.tips.divide: Creates evenly spaced point objects or blocks along the length or perimeter of an object
Ribbon.tips.measuresegments: Creates point objects or blocks at measured intervals along the length or perimeter of an object
Ribbon.tips.region: Converts an object that encloses an area into a region object
Ribbon.tips.move: Moves objects a specified distance in a specified direction
Ribbon.tips.copy: Copies objects a specified distance in a specified direction
Ribbon.tips.stretch: Stretches objects crossed by a selection window or polygon
Ribbon.tips.rotate: Rotates objects around a base point
Ribbon.tips.mirror: Creates a mirrored copy of selected objects
Ribbon.tips.scale: Enlarges or reduces selected objects, keeping the proportions of the object the same after scaling
Ribbon.tips.trim: Trims objects to meet the edges of other objects
Ribbon.tips.extend: Extends objects to meet the edges of other objects
Ribbon.tips.fillet: Rounds and fillets the edges of objects
Ribbon.tips.array: Distributes object copies into any combination of rows, columns, and levels.
Ribbon.tips.arraypath: Evenly distributes object copies along a path or a portion of a path.
Ribbon.tips.arraypolar: Evenly distributes object copies in a circular pattern around a center point or axis of rotation.
Ribbon.tips.explode: Breaks a compound object into its component objects
Ribbon.tips.offset: Creates concentric circles, parallel lines, and parallel curves
Ribbon.tips.splinedit: Edits a spline or spline-fit polyline
Ribbon.tips.break: Breaks the selected object between two points
Ribbon.tips.breakatpoint: Breaks the selected object at a single point
Ribbon.tips.join: Joins similar objects to form a single, unbroken object
Ribbon.tips.text: Displays text on screen as it is entered
Ribbon.tips.dimradius: Creates a radius dimension for a circle or an arc
Ribbon.tips.dimdiameter: Creates a diameter dimension for a circle or an arc
Ribbon.tips.textStyle: Creates, modifies, or specifies text styles
Ribbon.tips.insert: Inserts a block or drawing into the current drawing
Ribbon.tips.block: Creates a block definition from selected objects
Ribbon.tips.attedit: Edits attributes in a block reference
Ribbon.tips.attdef: Creates an attribute definition for storing data in a block
Ribbon.tips.matchprop: Applies the properties of a selected object to other objects
Ribbon.tips.list: Displays property data for selected objects
Ribbon.tips.measure: Measures the distance between two points or along a polyline
Ribbon.tips.id: Displays the UCS coordinate values of a specified location
Ribbon.tips.ptype: Specifies the display style and size of point objects
Ribbon.tips.paste: Pastes objects from the Clipboard into the current drawing
Ribbon.tips.cutclip: Copies selected objects to the Clipboard and removes them from the drawing
Ribbon.tips.copyclip: Copies selected objects to the Clipboard
Ribbon.tips.copybase: Copies selected objects to the Clipboard along with a specified base point
Ribbon.tips.createBlock: Creates a block definition from selected objects
Ribbon.tips.dimspace: Adjusts the spacing between linear dimensions or angular dimensions
Ribbon.tips.dimensionUpdate: Updates dimension objects with the current dimension style
Ribbon.tips.dimcontinue: Creates a dimension that starts from an extension line of a previously created dimension
Ribbon.tips.dimbaseline: Continues a linear, angular, or ordinate dimension from the baseline of the previous or selected dimension
Ribbon.tips.ucsIcon: Turns on or off display of the UCS icon
Ribbon.tips.viewCube: Turns on or off the display of the View Cube.

Ribbon.tips.ucsY: Rotates the user coordinate system about the Y axis

Ribbon.tips.ucsZAxis: Aligns the user coordinate system to a specified positive Z axis
Ribbon.tips.ucs3Point: Defines a new user coordinate system using three points
Ribbon.tips.ucsView: Aligns the XY plane of the user coordinate system with the screen
Ribbon.tips.ucsObject: Aligns the user coordinate system to a selected object
Ribbon.tips.ucsFace: Aligns the user coordinate system to a face on a 3D solid
Ribbon.tips.propertiesPalette: Opens or closes the Properties palette
Ribbon.tips.blocksPalette: Opens or closes the Blocks palette

Ribbon.tips.orbit: Rotates the view in 3D space, but constrained to horizontal and vertical orbit only
Ribbon.tips.zoomExtents: Zooms to display the maximum extents of all objects
Ribbon.tips.zoomWindow: Zooms to display an area specified by a rectangular window
Ribbon.tips.zoomPrevious: Zooms to display the previous view
Ribbon.tips.zoomIn: Zooms to increase the magnification of the current view by a factor of 2
Ribbon.tips.zoomOut: Zooms to decrease the magnification of the current view by a factor of 2
Ribbon.tips.extrude: Creates a 3D solid or surface by extruding a 2D or 3D curve
Ribbon.tips.revolve: Creates a 3D solid or surface by sweeping a 2D or 3D curve around an axis
Ribbon.tips.filletedge: Rounds and fillets the edges of solid objects
Ribbon.tips.chamferedge: Bevels the edges of solid objects
Ribbon.tips.slice: Creates new 3D solids and surfaces by slicing, or dividing, existing objects
Ribbon.tips.union: Combines selected 3D solids or 2D regions by addition
Ribbon.tips.subtract: Combines selected 3D solids or 2D regions by subtraction
Ribbon.tips.intersect: Creates a 3D solid or 2D region from selected overlapping solids or regions
Ribbon.tips.solideditextrude: Extrudes selected planar faces of a 3D solid by a specified distance or along a path
Ribbon.tips.solidedittaper: Tapers a face on a 3D solid at a specified angle
Ribbon.tips.solideditmove: Moves a face on 3D solids in a specified distance and direction
Ribbon.tips.solideditcopy: Copies faces from a 3D solid resulting in regions or solid bodies
Ribbon.tips.solideditoffset: Offsets selected faces of a 3D solid by a specified distance, changing its shape
Ribbon.tips.solideditrotate: Rotates selected faces on a 3D solid around a specified axis
Ribbon.tips.solideditdelete: Deletes faces, including fillets or chamfers, on a 3D solid

Ribbon.tips.dimensionsDiameter: Creates a diameter dimension for a circle or an arc

Ribbon.tips.view3d: Aligns the XY plane of the user coordinate system with the screen

Ribbon.tips.attModeOff: Makes all block attributes invisible, overriding the original visibility settings

Ribbon.tips.color: Provides a choice of colors to make current if no objects are selected, or changes the color of selected objects
Ribbon.tips.lineweight: Provides a choice of lineweights to make current if no objects are selected, or changes the lineweight of selected objects
Ribbon.tips.linetype: Provides a choice of linetypes to make current if no objects are selected, or changes the linetype of selected objects
Ribbon.tips.textStyleList: Provides a choice of text styles defined in the drawing to make current
Ribbon.tips.dimensionStyleList: Provides a choice of dimension styles defined in the drawing to make current
Ribbon.tips.visualStyleList: Provides a choice of visual styles defined in the drawing to make current
Ribbon.tips.arrayRowElevation: Specifies the incremental elevation between rows.
Ribbon.tips.arrayLevelTotal: Specifies the total distance between the first and last levels.
Ribbon.tips.arrayFillAngle: Specifies the angle between the first and last item in the array.
Ribbon.tips.arrayPathItems: Specifies the number of items.  Allows the number of items to be automatically calculated from the length of the path curve and the distance between items.
Ribbon.tips.arrayAssociative: Controls whether an associative array object is created.
Ribbon.tips.arrayRotateItems: Controls whether items are rotated as they are arrayed.
Ribbon.tips.arrayDirection: Controls whether to create a counter-clockwise or clockwise array.
Ribbon.tips.arrayDivide: Redistributes items to divide evenly along the length of the path.
Ribbon.tips.arrayMeasure: Maintains current item spacing when the path is edited, or when the number of items is edited through grips or the Properties palette.
Ribbon.tips.arrayAlignItems: Specifies whether to align each item to be tangent to the path direction. Alignment is relative to the orientation of the first item.
Ribbon.extended.line: With LINE, you can create a series of contiguous line segments. Each segment is a line object that can be edited separately.
Ribbon.extended.polyline: A 2D polyline is a connected sequence of segments created as a single planar object. You can create straight line segments, arc segments, or a combination of the two.
Ribbon.extended.arcsce:
The distance between the start point and the center determines the radius. The endpoint is determined by a line from the center that passes through the third point.

The resulting arc is always created counterclockwise from the start point.
Ribbon.extended.arccse:
The distance between the start point and the center determines the radius. The endpoint is determined by a line from the center that passes through the third point.

The resulting arc is always created counterclockwise from the start point.
Ribbon.extended.rectangle: Creates a rectangular polyline from the specified rectangle parameters (length, width, rotation) and type of corners (fillet, chamfer, or square).
Ribbon.extended.polygon: You can specify the different parameters of the polygon including the number of sides. The difference between the inscribed and circumscribed options is shown.
Ribbon.extended.ellipsecenter: Creates an ellipse using a center point, the endpoint of the first axis, and the length of the second axis. You can specify the distances by clicking a location at the desired distance or by entering a value for the length.
Ribbon.extended.ellipse: The first two points of the ellipse determine the location and length of the first axis. The third point determines the distance between the center of the ellipse and the end point of the second axis.
Ribbon.extended.ellipsearc: The first two points of the elliptical arc determine the location and length of the first axis. The third point determines the distance between the center of the elliptical arc and the endpoint of the second axis. The fourth and fifth points are the start and end angles.
Ribbon.extended.hatch: Choose from several methods to specify the boundaries of a hatch.Specify a point in an area that is enclosed by objects.Select objects that enclose an area.Specify boundary points using the -HATCH Draw option.Drag a hatch pattern into an enclosed area from a tool palette or DesignCenter.
Ribbon.extended.xline: Lines that extend to infinity, such as xlines, can be used to create construction and reference lines, and for trimming boundaries.
Ribbon.extended.ray: Lines that extend to infinity in one direction, known as rays, can be used as references for creating other objects.
Ribbon.extended.point: You can use MEASURE and DIVIDE to create points along an object. Use DDPTYPE to specify point size and styles easily.
Ribbon.extended.divide: Use DDPTYPE to set the style and size of all point objects in a drawing.
Ribbon.extended.measuresegments: Use DDPTYPE to set the style and size of all point objects in a drawing.
Ribbon.extended.region:
Regions are two-dimensional areas you create from closed shapes or loops. Closed polylines, lines, and curves are valid selections. Curves include circular arcs, circles, elliptical arcs, ellipses, and splines.

You can combine several regions into a single, complex region.
Ribbon.extended.wipeout: Creates a polygonal area that masks underlying objects with the current background color. The wipeout area is bounded by a frame that you can turn on or off. You can also choose to display the frame on screen and have it hidden for plotting.
Ribbon.extended.polyline3d: A 3D polyline is a connected sequence of straight line segments created as a single object. 3D polylines can be non-coplanar; however, they cannot include arc segments.
Ribbon.extended.move: Use coordinates, grid snaps, object snaps, and other tools to move objects with precision.
Ribbon.extended.copy: With the COPYMODE system variable, you can control whether multiple copies are created automatically.
Ribbon.extended.stretch: Objects that are partially enclosed by a crossing window are stretched. Objects that are completely enclosed within the crossing window, or that are selected individually, are moved rather than stretched. Some types of objects such as circles, ellipses, and blocks, cannot be stretched.
Ribbon.extended.rotate: You can rotate selected objects around a base point to an absolute angle.
Ribbon.extended.mirror: You can create objects that represent half of a drawing, select them, and mirror them across a specified line to create the other half.
Ribbon.extended.scale: To scale an object, specify a base point and a scale factor. The base point acts as the center of the scaling operation and remains stationary. A scale factor greater than 1 enlarges the object. A scale factor between 0 and 1 shrinks the object.
Ribbon.extended.trim: To trim objects, select the objects to be trimmed individually, press and drag to start a freehand selection path, or pick two empty locations to specify a crossing Fence. All objects automatically act as cutting edges. Selected objects that can't be trimmed are deleted instead.
Ribbon.extended.extend: To extend objects, select the objects to be extended individually, press and drag to start a freehand selection path, or pick two empty locations to specify a crossing Fence. All objects automatically act as boundary edges.
Ribbon.extended.fillet: In the example, an arc is created that is tangent to both of the selected lines. The lines are trimmed to the ends of the arc. To create a sharp corner instead, enter a radius of zero.
Ribbon.extended.chamfer: The distances and angles that you specify are applied in the order that you select the objects.
Ribbon.extended.array: Creates an array of rows and columns of copies of the selected object.
Ribbon.extended.arraypath: The path can be a line, polyline, 3D polyline, spline, helix, arc, circle, or ellipse.
Ribbon.extended.arraypolar: Creates an array by copying the selected objects around a specified center point or axis of rotation.
Ribbon.extended.erase: Instead of selecting objects to erase, you can enter an option, such as L to erase the last object drawn, p to erase the previous selection set, or ALL to erase all objects. You can also enter ? to get a list of all options.
Ribbon.extended.explode: Explodes a compound object when you want to modify its components separately. Objects that can be exploded include blocks, polylines, and regions, among others.
Ribbon.extended.offset: You can offset an object at a specified distance or through a point. After you offset objects, you can trim and extend them as an efficient method to create drawings containing many parallel lines and curves.
Ribbon.extended.pedit: Common uses for PEDIT include joining 2D polylines, converting lines and arcs into 2D polylines, and converting polylines into curves that approximate B-splines (spline-fit polylines).
Ribbon.extended.splinedit: Modifies the data that defines a spline, such as the number and weight of control vertices, the fit tolerance, and the starting and ending tangents.
Ribbon.extended.break: You can create a gap between two specified points on an object, breaking it into two objects. If the points are off of an object, they are automatically projected on to the object. break is often used to create space for a block or text.
Ribbon.extended.breakatpoint: Valid objects include lines, open polylines, and arcs. Closed objects such as circles cannot be broken at a single point.
Ribbon.extended.join: Combines a series of finite linear and open curved objects at their common endpoints to create a single 2D or 3D object. The type of object that results depends on the types of objects selected, the type of object selected first, and whether the objects are coplanar.
Ribbon.extended.mtext: You can create several paragraphs of text as a single multiline text (mtext) object. With the built-in editor, you can format the text appearance, columns, and boundaries.
Ribbon.extended.text: You can use single-line text to create one or more lines of text, where each text line is an independent object that you can move, format, or otherwise modify. Right-click in the text box to select options on the shortcut menu.
Ribbon.extended.dimlinear: Creates a linear dimension with a horizontal, vertical, or rotated dimension line. This command replaces the DIMHORIZONTAL and DIMVERTICAL commands.
Ribbon.extended.dimaligned: Creates a linear dimension that is aligned with the origin points of the extension lines.
Ribbon.extended.dimangular: Measures the angle between selected objects or 3 points. Objects that can be selected include arcs, circles, and lines, among others.
Ribbon.extended.dimradius: Measures the radius of a selected circle or arc and displays the dimension text with a radius symbol in front of it. You can use grips to reposition the resulting radius dimension easily.
Ribbon.extended.dimdiameter: Measures the diameter of a selected circle or arc, and displays the dimension text with a diameter symbol in front of it. You can use grips to easily reposition the resulting diameter dimension.
Ribbon.extended.textStyle: You can specify the current text style to determine the appearance of all new text. A text style includes the font, size, obliquing angle, orientation, and other text characteristics.
Ribbon.extended.dimensionStyle: A dimension style is a named collection of dimension settings that control the appearance of dimensions. You create dimension styles to specify the format of dimensions quickly, and to ensure that dimensions conform to standards.
Ribbon.extended.insert: A good practice is to insert a block from a block library. A block library can be a drawing file that stores related block definitions or it can be a folder that contains related drawing files, each of which can be inserted as a block. With either method, blocks are standardized and accessible to multiple users.
Ribbon.extended.block: You create a block definition by selecting objects, specifying an insertion point, and giving it a name.
Ribbon.extended.attedit: Edits the values, text options, and properties of each attribute in a block.
Ribbon.extended.attdef: An attribute is an object that is created and included with a block definition. Attributes can store data such as part numbers, product names, and so on.
Ribbon.extended.matchprop: The types of properties that can be applied include color, layer, linetype, linetype scale, lineweight, plot style, transparency, and other specified properties.
Ribbon.extended.list: You can use LIST to display and then copy the properties of selected objects to a text file.
Ribbon.extended.measure:
In model space, changes in X, Y, and Z component distances and angles are measured in 3D relative to the current UCS.

In paper space, distances are normally reported in 2D paper space units. However, when using object snaps on model space objects that are displayed in a single viewport, distances are reported as 2D model space distances projected onto a plane parallel to your screen.
Ribbon.extended.measurearea: Several commands are available to provide area information including AREA, MEASUREGEOM, and MASSPROP. Alternatively, use BOUNDARY to create a closed polyline or region. Then use LIST or the Properties palette to find the area.
Ribbon.extended.id: ID lists the X, Y, and Z values of the specified point and stores the coordinate of the specified point as the last point. You can reference the last point by entering @ at the next prompt that requests a point.
Ribbon.extended.paste: When you copy objects to the Clipboard, information is stored in all available formats. When you paste the Clipboard contents into a drawing, the format that retains the most information is used. You can also use Copy and Paste to transfer objects between drawings.
Ribbon.extended.cutclip: When you want to use objects from a drawing file in another application, you can cut these objects to the Clipboard and then paste them into another application. You can also use Cut and Paste to transfer objects between drawings.
Ribbon.extended.copyclip: When you copy objects to the Clipboard, information is stored in all available formats. When you paste the Clipboard contents into a drawing, the format that retains the most information is used. You can also use Copy and Paste to transfer objects between drawings.
Ribbon.extended.copybase: The selected objects are copied to the Clipboard.Use PASTECLIP to move the copied objects from the Clipboard to a location in the same document or to another document.When you paste an object copied with COPYBASE, it is placed relative to the specified base point.
Ribbon.extended.createBlock: You create a block definition by selecting objects, specifying an insertion point, and giving it a name.
Ribbon.extended.dimspace: The spacing between parallel dimension lines is made equal. You can also make the dimension lines of a series of linear or angular dimensions line up by using a spacing value of 0.
Ribbon.extended.dimensionUpdate: You can save or restore dimensioning system variables to a selected dimension style.
Ribbon.extended.dimcontinue: Automatically continues creating additional dimensions from the last linear, angular, or ordinate dimension created, or from a selected extension line. The dimension lines are lined up automatically.
Ribbon.extended.dimbaseline: The default spacing between baseline dimensions can be set from the Dimension Style Manager, Lines tab, Baseline Spacing (DIMDLI system variable).
Ribbon.extended.ucsWorld: The WCS is a fixed Cartesian coordinate system. All objects are defined by their WCS coordinates, and the WCS and the UCS are coincident in a new drawing. However, it is usually more convenient to create and edit objects based on the UCS, which can be customized to suit your drawing or modeling needs.
Ribbon.extended.ucsX: Point your right thumb in the positive direction of the X axis and curl your fingers. Your fingers indicate the positive rotation direction about the axis.
Ribbon.extended.ucsY: Point your right thumb in the positive direction of the Y axis and curl your fingers. Your fingers indicate the positive rotation direction about the axis.
Ribbon.extended.ucsZ: Point your right thumb in the positive direction of the Z axis and curl your fingers. Your fingers indicate the positive rotation direction about the axis.
Ribbon.extended.ucsPrevious: You can steps back through the last 10 UCS settings in the current session. UCS settings are stored independently for model space and paper space.
Ribbon.extended.ucsOrigin: Shifts the user coordinate system origin point (0,0,0) to facilitate entering absolute coordinates, creating ordinate dimensions, or setting the work plane in 3D.
Ribbon.extended.ucsZAxis: The UCS origin is moved to the first point and its positive Z axis passes through the second point.
Ribbon.extended.ucs3Point: The three points specify an origin point, a point on the positive X axis, and a point on the positive XY plane.
Ribbon.extended.ucsView: Aligns the XY plane of the UCS to a plane perpendicular to your viewing direction. The origin point remains unchanged, but the X and Y axes become horizontal and vertical.
Ribbon.extended.ucsObject: Move the cursor over an object to see a preview of how the UCS will align, and click to place the UCS. In most cases, the UCS origin will be located at the endpoint that is nearest to the specified point, the X axis will align to an edge or tangent to a curve, and the Z axis will align perpendicular to the object.
Ribbon.extended.ucsFace: Move the cursor over a face to see a preview of how the UCS will be aligned.
Ribbon.extended.pan: Position the cursor at the start location and press the mouse button down. Drag the cursor to the new location. You can also press the mouse scroll wheel or middle button down and drag the cursor to pan.
Ribbon.extended.orbit: Selecting one of more objects before starting this command limits the display to those objects only.
Ribbon.extended.zoomExtents: You can change the magnification of a view by zooming in and out, which is similar to zooming in and out with a camera. Using ZOOM does not change the absolute size of objects in the drawing. It changes only the magnification of the view.
Ribbon.extended.zoomWindow: You can change the magnification of a view by zooming in and out, which is similar to zooming in and out with a camera. Using ZOOM does not change the absolute size of objects in the drawing. It changes only the magnification of the view.
Ribbon.extended.zoomPrevious: You can change the magnification of a view by zooming in and out, which is similar to zooming in and out with a camera. Using ZOOM does not change the absolute size of objects in the drawing. It changes only the magnification of the view.
Ribbon.extended.zoomIn: You can change the magnification of a view by zooming in and out, which is similar to zooming in and out with a camera. Using ZOOM does not change the absolute size of objects in the drawing. It changes only the magnification of the view.
Ribbon.extended.zoomOut: You can change the magnification of a view by zooming in and out, which is similar to zooming in and out with a camera. Using ZOOM does not change the absolute size of objects in the drawing. It changes only the magnification of the view.
Ribbon.extended.box: The base of the box is always drawn parallel to the XY plane of the current UCS (work plane). The height of the box is specified in the Z-axis direction. You can enter both positive and negative values for the height.
Ribbon.extended.cylinder: In the illustration, the cylinder was created using a center point (1), a point on the radius (2), and a point for the height (3). The base of the cylinder is always on a plane parallel with the workplane. You can control the smoothness of curved 3D solids, such as a cylinder, in a shaded or hidden visual style with the FACETRES system variable.
Ribbon.extended.cone: Creates a 3D solid with a circular or elliptical base that tapers symmetrically to a point or to a circular or elliptical planar face. You can control the smoothness of 3D curved solids, such as a cone, in a shaded or hidden visual style with the FACETRES system variable.
Ribbon.extended.sphere: You can create a sphere by specifying a center point and a point on the radius. You can control the smoothness of curved 3D solids, such as a sphere, in a shaded or hidden visual style with the FACETRES system variable.
Ribbon.extended.pyramid: By default, a pyramid is defined by the center of the base point, a point on the middle of the edge, and another point that determines the height.
Ribbon.extended.wedge: The direction of the taper is always in the positive X-axis direction of the UCS.
Ribbon.extended.torus: You can create a torus by specifying the center, then the radius or diameter of the torus, and then the radius or diameter of the tube that surrounds the torus. You can control the smoothness of curved 3D solids, such as a torus, in a shaded or hidden visual style with the FACETRES system variable.
Ribbon.extended.presspull: Get visual feedback as you move the cursor after selecting a 2D object, an area formed by a closed boundary or a 3D solid face. The press or pull behavior responds to the type of object you select to create extrusions and offsets. In this example, the area between two polylines is pulled to create a 3D solid wall.
Ribbon.extended.filletedge: You can select more than one edge. Enter a value for the fillet radius or click and drag the fillet grip.
Ribbon.extended.chamferedge: You can select more than one edge at a time, as long as they belong to the same face. Enter a value for the chamfer distance or click and drag the chamfer grips.
Ribbon.extended.slice: The cutting plane is defined with 2 or 3 points, by specifying a major plane of the UCS, or by selecting a surface object (but not a mesh). Either one or both sides of the sliced 3D solids can be retained.
Ribbon.extended.union: You can combine two or more 3D solids, surfaces, or 2D regions into a single, composite 3D solid, surface, or region. You must select the same type of objects to combine.
Ribbon.extended.subtract: Select the objects that you want to keep, press Enter, then select the objects that you want to subtract.
Ribbon.extended.intersect: You can extrude 2D profiles and then intersect them to create a complex model efficiently.
Ribbon.extended.solideditextrude: Entering a positive value extrudes the face outward; entering a positive taper angle bevels the edges to the face. The Path option extrudes the face along a selected line or curve. For major changes along a curve, consider using the Sweep command.
Ribbon.extended.solidedittaper: A positive angle tapers the face in, and a negative angle tapers the face out. The default angle, 0, extrudes the face perpendicular to its plane. All selected faces in the selection set are tapered to the same value.
Ribbon.extended.solideditmove: You can change the shape of the object by moving its faces. This option is recommended for minor adjustments.
Ribbon.extended.solideditcopy: Creates a new object with the original orientation and profile of the face. The result can be used as a reference to create a new 3D solid.
Ribbon.extended.solideditoffset: A positive value increases the size of the 3D solid, a negative value decreases the size. Adjacent faces are stretched but maintain their angles relative to the offset face.
Ribbon.extended.solideditrotate: You can change the shape of the object by rotating its faces. This option is recommended for minor adjustments.
Ribbon.extended.solideditdelete: Use this option to remove and later modify filleted and chamfered edges. The face is not deleted if the change results in a non-valid 3D solid.
Ribbon.extended.insertAttedit: Edits the values, text options, and properties of each attribute in a block.
Ribbon.extended.defineAttributes: An attribute is an object that is created and included with a block definition. Attributes can store data such as part numbers, product names, and so on.
Ribbon.extended.multilineText: You can create several paragraphs of text as a single multiline text (mtext) object. With the built-in editor, you can format the text appearance, columns, and boundaries.
Ribbon.extended.dimensionsLinear: Creates a linear dimension with a horizontal, vertical, or rotated dimension line. This command replaces the DIMHORIZONTAL and DIMVERTICAL commands.
Ribbon.extended.dimensionsAligned: Creates a linear dimension that is aligned with the origin points of the extension lines.
Ribbon.extended.dimensionsAngular: Measures the angle between selected objects or 3 points. Objects that can be selected include arcs, circles, and lines, among others.
Ribbon.extended.dimensionsRadius: Measures the radius of a selected circle or arc and displays the dimension text with a radius symbol in front of it. You can use grips to reposition the resulting radius dimension easily.
Ribbon.extended.dimensionsDiameter: Measures the diameter of a selected circle or arc, and displays the dimension text with a diameter symbol in front of it. You can use grips to easily reposition the resulting diameter dimension.
Ribbon.extended.axisX: Point your right thumb in the positive direction of the X axis and curl your fingers. Your fingers indicate the positive rotation direction about the axis.
Ribbon.extended.axisY: Point your right thumb in the positive direction of the Y axis and curl your fingers. Your fingers indicate the positive rotation direction about the axis.
Ribbon.extended.axisZ: Point your right thumb in the positive direction of the Z axis and curl your fingers. Your fingers indicate the positive rotation direction about the axis.
Ribbon.extended.view3d: Aligns the XY plane of the UCS to a plane perpendicular to your viewing direction. The origin point remains unchanged, but the X and Y axes become horizontal and vertical.
Ribbon.extended.world: The WCS is a fixed Cartesian coordinate system. All objects are defined by their WCS coordinates, and the WCS and the UCS are coincident in a new drawing. However, it is usually more convenient to create and edit objects based on the UCS, which can be customized to suit your drawing or modeling needs.
Ribbon.extended.previous: You can steps back through the last 10 UCS settings in the current session. UCS settings are stored independently for model space and paper space.
Ribbon.extended.propertiesLauncher:
When more than one object is selected, only those properties common to all selected objects are displayed.

When no objects are selected, only the current settings of general properties are displayed.
Ribbon.menu.empty: The Ribbon does not have any tabs or panels currently loaded.
